segments.en: Hello, English learners.
segments.zh: 各位英语学习者，大家好。

segments.en: Welcome back to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 欢迎回到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: And my name is Catherine.
segments.zh: 我叫 Catherine。

segments.en: And today we're talking about being on the road.
segments.zh: 今天我们谈论的是在路上。

segments.en: Yeah, we're going to be on the road, but we're going to encounter a little bit of a car problems.
segments.zh: 对，我们要上路，不过会遇到一点汽车故障。

segments.en: My favorite kind.
segments.zh: 我最喜欢的那种。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: I think it's happened to everyone.
segments.zh: 我想这发生在每个人身上。

segments.en: You're on the road or maybe you're coming back from work, you get a flat tire or something happens to your car, right?
segments.zh: 你可能正在路上，也可能在下班回家的途中，突然爆胎了，或者车出了别的问题，对吧？

segments.en: And it's always when you're in a rush.
segments.zh: 总是在你匆忙的时候。

segments.en: And most of the time it's raining.
segments.zh: 而且大部分时间都在下雨。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: It's snowing.
segments.zh: 正在下雪。

segments.en: So all of the circumstances definitely, well, they don't help.
segments.zh: 所以所有情况肯定，好吧，它们没有帮助。

segments.en: Let's just say.
segments.zh: 让我们说。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So before we listen to this dialogue, let's take a look at some of the words in today's vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 听对话之前，我们先在今天的“词汇预习”中看看几个单词。

segments.en: Vocabulary preview.
segments.zh: 词汇预习。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So we're going to take a look at two words.
segments.zh: 所以我们要看两个词。

segments.en: They're kind of strange.
segments.zh: 他们有点奇怪。

segments.en: I don't know, kind of difficult to understand.
segments.zh: 我不知道，有点难以理解。

segments.en: So that's what we're going to explain them.
segments.zh: 所以这就是我们要解释的。

segments.en: The first one is spew, to spew.
segments.zh: 第一个是吐，吐。

segments.en: It's a verb, okay?
segments.zh: 这是一个动词，好吗？

segments.en: To spew.
segments.zh: 吐。

segments.en: Well, what can spew?
segments.zh: 嗯，什么可以吐？

segments.en: Volcano can spew.
segments.zh: 火山可以喷。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: An engine can spew.
segments.zh: 发动机可以喷。

segments.en: A person can spew.
segments.zh: 一个人可以吐。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: That's not very nice.
segments.zh: 这不是很好。

segments.en: No.
segments.zh: 不。

segments.en: So basically it's to like expel or to shoot out from your mouth or something liquid.
segments.zh: 所以基本上它是喜欢驱逐或从你的嘴或液体中射出。

segments.en: So in the case of a person, right?
segments.zh: 所以在一个人的情况下，对吧？

segments.en: So if a person spews, it means a person throws up, but it's usually very forceful.
segments.zh: 所以如果一个人吐了，就意味着一个人呕吐，但它通常非常有力。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: It's very messy.
segments.zh: 这是非常混乱的。

segments.en: A volcano can spew lava.
segments.zh: 火山可以喷出熔岩。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So a volcano is spewing lava.
segments.zh: 所以一座火山正在喷出熔岩。

segments.en: Now for the next word that we have, it's an informal way of saying that something is broken.
segments.zh: 现在对于我们的下一个词，这是一种非正式的说法，说某事被打破了。

segments.en: You could say it's busted.
segments.zh: 你可以说它被破坏了。

segments.en: It's busted.
segments.zh: 它被破坏了。

segments.en: My DVD player is busted.
segments.zh: 我的 DVD 播放器坏了。

segments.en: Man, my phone is busted.
segments.zh: 伙计，我的手机坏了。

segments.en: So it's an informal way, very popular, very common I would say, to describe that something is not working.
segments.zh: 所以，这是形容东西坏了的一种非正式说法，我觉得很流行，也很常见。

segments.en: I don't think many people actually say, well, it's broken or it's damaged.
segments.zh: 我不认为很多人真的说，好吧，它坏了或损坏了。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: They're pretty much mixed I think, but you will definitely hear busted if you're talking to native English speakers.
segments.zh: 我觉得这几种说法都会混着用，但如果你和英语母语者聊天，肯定会听到busted。

segments.en: Or even like, for example, your arm.
segments.zh: 甚至喜欢，例如，你的手臂。

segments.en: He's got a busted arm.
segments.zh: 他的手臂破裂了。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So busted.
segments.zh: 如此破产。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So let's listen to our dialogue for the first time.
segments.zh: 所以让我们第一次听我们的对话。

segments.en: Let's see what's going on with this car trouble and then we'll come back and explain some things.
segments.zh: 让我们看看这辆汽车的麻烦是怎么回事，然后我们会回来解释一些事情。

segments.en: Howdy.
segments.zh: 你好。

segments.en: Nice car.
segments.zh: 好车。

segments.en: What seems to be the problem?
segments.zh: 请问有什么问题？

segments.en: I don't know.
segments.zh: 我不知道。

segments.en: This stupid old car started spewing white smoke and it just died on me.
segments.zh: 这辆破旧的车开始冒白烟，然后就突然熄火了。

segments.en: Luckily I managed to start it up and drive it here.
segments.zh: 幸好我还是发动了车，把它开到这里来了。

segments.en: What do you think it is?
segments.zh: 你认为它是什么？

segments.en: Not sure yet.
segments.zh: 还不确定。

segments.en: How about you pop the hood and we could take a look?
segments.zh: 你把引擎盖打开，我们看看好吗？

segments.en: Mm.
segments.zh: 嗯。

segments.en: It doesn't look good.
segments.zh: 情况不妙。

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: My daddy gave me this car for my birthday last month.
segments.zh: 这辆车是上个月爸爸送我的生日礼物。

segments.en: It's brand new.
segments.zh: 这是全新的。

segments.en: Well, missy, the white smoke that you saw is steam from the radiator.
segments.zh: 嗯，小姐，你看到的白烟是散热器的蒸汽。

segments.en: You overheated your engine so now the pistons are busted, and so is your transmission.
segments.zh: 发动机过热了，所以现在活塞坏了，变速箱也坏了。

segments.en: You should have called us and we could have towed you over here when your car died.
segments.zh: 车熄火时你就该打电话给我们，我们可以把车拖过来。

segments.en: Ugh. So, how long is this going to take?
segments.zh: 呃。 那么，这需要多长时间？

segments.en: An hour?
segments.zh: 一个小时？

segments.en: I'm afraid a bit more than that.
segments.zh: 恐怕得更久一些。

segments.en: We need to order the spare parts, take apart your electrical system, fuel pump, and engine, and then put it back together again.
segments.zh: 我们需要订购备件，把你的电路系统、燃油泵和发动机拆开，再重新装好。

segments.en: You're going to have to leave it here for at least, uh, two weeks.
segments.zh: 你至少要把它留在这里，呃，两个星期。

segments.en: What?
segments.zh: 什么？

segments.en: How am I supposed to go to school?
segments.zh: 我该怎么去上学？

segments.en: Or go shopping?
segments.zh: 那买东西怎么办？

segments.en: This is not happening.
segments.zh: 怎么会这样！

segments.en: So if I were the mechanic, I would not be very happy to be dealing with someone like this girl.
segments.zh: 所以如果我是机械师，我不会很高兴与像这个女孩这样的人打交道。

segments.en: I think it's, uh, well maybe it's a little bit stereotypical that we put it as a girl, because guys and girls, so many people don't know anything about cars or mechanics.
segments.zh: 我觉得，把这个角色设成女生，可能有点刻板印象了，因为无论男女，很多人都不懂汽车或机械。

segments.en: And in the States, there's a lot of female mechanics too, so it's, you know, it's mixed.
segments.zh: 在美国，也有很多女性机械师，所以，你知道，它是混合的。

segments.en: But definitely it's something that happens all the time, and probably the mechanic will overcharge her as well, because apparently she doesn't know what she's doing.
segments.zh: 不过这种事确实经常发生，而且修车师傅可能还会多收她的钱，因为她显然不懂这些。

segments.en: And that's one of the reasons we want to give you the vocabulary to deal with these situations.
segments.zh: 这就是我们希望为您提供处理这些情况的词汇的原因之一。

segments.en: So let's look at some of those car words in today's Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以让我们看看今天的语言外卖中的一些汽车词。

segments.en: Alright, so we're going to take a look at very specific words related to cars and the engines and everything.
segments.zh: 好，我们来看看一些与汽车、发动机等有关的专业词汇。

segments.en: So let's start with the first one.
segments.zh: 所以让我们从第一个开始。

segments.en: Radiator.
segments.zh: 散热器。

segments.en: Radiator. Alright, so the radiator of the car.
segments.zh: 散热器。 好吧，所以汽车的散热器。

segments.en: So a radiator is something that you normally find in the front of the car near the engine.
segments.zh: 因此，散热器是您通常在汽车前部靠近发动机的地方找到的东西。

segments.en: It usually gets very, very hot, right?
segments.zh: 它通常会变得非常非常热，对吧？

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So one of the big issues is radiators getting too hot because there's no way to cool them down.
segments.zh: 所以一大问题是散热器太热了，因为没有办法让它们冷却下来。

segments.en: Mm-hmm. So if you live in a place that's very hot, the radiator keeps your engine cool because it has water in it.
segments.zh: 嗯。如果你住的地方很热，散热器里的水能帮助发动机保持凉爽。

segments.en: So if it overheats, or maybe you didn't put enough water in there, then it'll start spewing steam like in this dialogue.
segments.zh: 所以，如果散热器过热，或者里面加的水不够，就会像对话里那样开始喷出蒸汽。

segments.en: And if you have a problem with your radiator, you could actually do a lot of damage to your engine, which is why this is important.
segments.zh: 而且散热器一旦有问题，可能会严重损坏发动机，所以这一点很重要。

segments.en: Exactly, and that's what happened in this dialogue.
segments.zh: 没错，这就是这次对话中发生的事情。

segments.en: So a radiator.
segments.zh: 所以是散热器。

segments.en: Now, because the radiator wasn't working well, it overheated the engine, and he said they had some busted pistons.
segments.zh: 因为散热器工作不正常，发动机过热了，所以他说有几个活塞坏了。

segments.en: So broken pistons.
segments.zh: 如此破碎的活塞。

segments.en: Pistons are important because they're kind of like valves that go up and down.
segments.zh: 活塞很重要，因为它们有点像上下波动的阀门。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: So inside your engine, you have mini explosions, and the pistons move up and down, and that's what actually moves your car.
segments.zh: 发动机里面会发生一次次小规模燃烧爆发，带动活塞上下运动，汽车就是这样被驱动的。

segments.en: Right.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: And so pistons, in general, are things in mechanics. So like a trumpet has pistons, things that go up and down and that allow for the flow of air.
segments.zh: 所以，活塞通常是一种机械部件。比如小号也有活塞，会上下运动，让空气通过。

segments.en: Air or something like that. Very good.
segments.zh: 空气或类似的东西。 非常好。

segments.en: So that's a piston.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个活塞。

segments.en: And, well, another very common mechanic term is the transmission.
segments.zh: 而且，另一个非常常见的机械术语是传输。

segments.en: Alright, so the transmission.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以传输。

segments.en: What happens if your transmission dies?
segments.zh: 如果您的传输死亡，会发生什么？

segments.en: Can you still drive?
segments.zh: 你还能开车吗？

segments.en: You basically can't move, or maybe you only have one gear or two gears.
segments.zh: 你基本上不能移动，或者你只有一个或两个齿轮。

segments.en: Alright, so think about transmission as coming from the word to transmit. That means to transfer.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以想想传输是从这个词传到传输的。 这意味着转移。

segments.en: So this is the part of the car that transfers energy or the power to actually move the car.
segments.zh: 所以这是汽车的部分，可以传递能量或动力来实际移动汽车。

segments.en: So the transmission.
segments.zh: 所以传输。

segments.en: And we've got the mechanic who says, well, we've got to order you some spare parts.
segments.zh: 我们有机械师说，好吧，我们必须为您订购一些备件。

segments.en: So first, let's look at the word spare.
segments.zh: 所以首先，让我们看看 Spare 这个词。

segments.en: What's another word for spare?
segments.zh: 备用的另一个词是什么？

segments.en: Additional, maybe extra.
segments.zh: 另外，也许是额外的。

segments.en: Right. So spare means extra. Parts are, well, pieces. So he's talking about ordering a new transmission, new pistons, things to replace the broken things.
segments.zh: 对，spare是“额外的、备用的”，parts就是“零件”。所以他是在说，要订购新的变速器、活塞等，来替换坏掉的部件。

segments.en: Spare parts.
segments.zh: 备件。

segments.en: So this is where you go to the mechanic to get some spare parts and get them installed.
segments.zh: 所以这是你去机械师那里获取一些备件并安装它们的地方。

segments.en: You probably don't have many spare parts at home, right? You got a transmission lying around.
segments.zh: 你家里可能没有很多备件，对吧？ 你周围有一个变速箱。

segments.en: Well, yeah, so spare parts.
segments.zh: 嗯，是的，所以备件。

segments.en: And the last word that we're going to take a look at is a fuel pump.
segments.zh: 我们要看看的最后一个词是燃油泵。

segments.en: Okay, so a pump is, you could have a bike pump.
segments.zh: 好的，所以泵是，你可以有一个自行车泵。

segments.en: A water pump.
segments.zh: 一个水泵。

segments.en: Water pump.
segments.zh: 水泵。

segments.en: So these are something, these are some things that we use very, very often.
segments.zh: 所以这些是一些东西，这些是我们非常非常经常使用的一些东西。

segments.en: But a fuel pump is something that allows gas, gasoline, to get into your engine.
segments.zh: 但是燃油泵是允许燃气、汽油进入发动机的东西。

segments.en: So it's basically a device that pushes gasoline into the engine so you can start.
segments.zh: 所以它基本上是一种将汽油推入发动机的装置，这样你就可以启动了。

segments.en: And that's the same thing with the water pump.
segments.zh: 这与水泵也是如此。

segments.en: It's a device that pushes water.
segments.zh: 它是一种推动水的设备。

segments.en: Or an air pump is something that pushes air into your tires and your bicycle.
segments.zh: 或者气泵是将空气推入轮胎和自行车的东西。

segments.en: Exactly. So a fuel pump, water pump, etc.
segments.zh: 没错。 所以燃油泵、水泵等。

segments.en: Wow, I feel like we know a lot about cars.
segments.zh: 哇，我觉得我们对汽车了解很多。

segments.en: Yeah, apparently we do.
segments.zh: 是的，显然我们这样做了。

segments.en: See? Alright, so now that we've taken a look at all of these great words, let's move on to a couple of phrases in Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 明白了吧？好，既然已经学了这些有用的词汇，接下来就在“流利表达”里学习几个短语。

segments.en: Alright, these are phrases that you hear sometimes when you're talking about electronics.
segments.zh: 好吧，这些是您在谈论电子产品时有时会听到的短语。

segments.en: But in today's lesson, we're also talking about specific car phrases.
segments.zh: 但在今天的课程中，我们也在谈论特定的汽车短语。

segments.en: So you're going to hear these all the time at the mechanics.
segments.zh: 所以你会一直在机械师那里听到这些。

segments.en: Right, and the first one is, the car suddenly died on me.
segments.zh: 是的，第一个是，汽车突然死在我身上。

segments.en: Alright, to die on.
segments.zh: 好吧，死去。

segments.en: So we keep these two words together, die on.
segments.zh: 所以我们把这两个词放在一起，死去。

segments.en: Oh man, so while you were driving, your car died.
segments.zh: 哦，伙计，所以当你开车的时候，你的车死了。

segments.en: It stopped moving.
segments.zh: 它停止了移动。

segments.en: So that means that it doesn't work anymore.
segments.zh: 所以这意味着它不再起作用了。

segments.en: And it's not only for cars, right? You can say my MP3 player died on me today.
segments.zh: 而且它不仅适用于汽车，对吧？ 你可以说我的 MP3 播放器今天死在我身上。

segments.en: Exactly, and what it means is, it's not like you left it and you forgot about it and you tried it again and it didn't work.
segments.zh: 没错，它不是说你把东西放在一边，后来忘了，再拿来用时发现它坏了。

segments.en: It means while you're using it, it dies.
segments.zh: 这意味着当你使用它时，它会死掉。

segments.en: It doesn't work.
segments.zh: 它不起作用。

segments.en: So I think this phrase is a good one to give some other examples.
segments.zh: 所以我认为这句话是一个很好的例子，可以举出一些其他的例子。

segments.en: So let's listen.
segments.zh: 那么我们来听听。

segments.en: So this next one is a phrase you hear, the first thing you hear maybe, when you tell someone you have a car problem.
segments.zh: 下一个短语，是你告诉别人汽车出了故障时，可能首先听到的一句话。

segments.en: Right, you tell them to pop the hood.
segments.zh: 对，你告诉他们弹出引擎盖。

segments.en: Or let's pop the hood.
segments.zh: 或者让我们弹出引擎盖。

segments.en: So this means let's open the front part of the car, the hood, to look at the engine, transmission, all those parts.
segments.zh: 意思就是打开汽车前面的引擎盖，看看发动机、变速器等部件。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So you can say open the hood, but the most common one is pop the hood.
segments.zh: 所以你可以说打开引擎盖，但最常见的一种是打开引擎盖。

segments.en: So the reason is because there is a little spring and you have to pull inside the car and it goes pop, and there's a little jump.
segments.zh: 之所以这样说，是因为那里有个小弹簧，你在车内拉一下开关，它就会“啪”地弹起一点。

segments.en: Yeah, exactly.
segments.zh: 对，没错。

segments.en: So it's literally popping.
segments.zh: 所以它确实是在弹出。

segments.en: Right, or you can also say the trunk, right, the back part of the car.
segments.zh: 对了，或者你也可以说后备箱，右，汽车的后部。

segments.en: Hey, can you pop the trunk for me?
segments.zh: 嘿，你能帮我弹出后备箱吗？

segments.en: I've got to put some stuff inside.
segments.zh: 我必须在里面放一些东西。

segments.en: Exactly, so pop the hood, pop the trunk.
segments.zh: 确切地说，打开引擎盖，弹出行李箱。

segments.en: And next we've got this girl actually, who's talking about her car because she just got this car.
segments.zh: 接下来我们实际上有了这个女孩，她在谈论她的车，因为她刚拿到这辆车。

segments.en: So what's another way to say it's a new car?
segments.zh: 那么说它是新车的另一种方式是什么？

segments.en: It's brand new.
segments.zh: 这是全新的。

segments.en: Is that more new than new?
segments.zh: 这比新的更新吗？

segments.en: It's like newer, newer than new.
segments.zh: 它就像更新，比新的更新。

segments.en: Alright, so brand, you think about brands like Ford or Gucci, these are brands, but brand new means she maybe got it like today.
segments.zh: 好，brand会让你想到福特、古驰这样的品牌，但brand new是说，她可能今天才买到这东西。

segments.en: So it's brand new, it's very, very new.
segments.zh: 所以它是全新的，它非常非常新。

segments.en: Did you see my brand new watch?
segments.zh: 你看到我全新的手表了吗？

segments.en: Oh, it is nice, did you get it? Alright, so brand new.
segments.zh: 哦，很好，你明白了吗？ 好吧，全新的。

segments.en: And well, the last phrase that we have for you today is to take apart something.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们今天为您准备的最后一句话是拆开一些东西。

segments.en: Alright, so this is very popular with young children, like they like to take things apart so they can find out how they work.
segments.zh: 小孩子很喜欢这样做，他们喜欢把东西拆开，看看它们是怎么运作的。

segments.en: But to take apart means to take all the pieces and to pull them out.
segments.zh: 但拆开意味着把所有的碎片都拉出来。

segments.en: Yeah, I used to do that a lot when I was a kid.
segments.zh: 是的，我小时候经常这样做。

segments.en: I used to take apart any electronic device to kind of see how it works and then I would try to put it back together again.
segments.zh: 我以前会拆开各种电子设备，看看它们怎么工作，然后再试着装回去。

segments.en: That's why you're so smart.
segments.zh: 这就是你如此聪明的原因。

segments.en: Well, it never really worked, it worked half the time.
segments.zh: 好吧，它从来没有真正工作过，它工作了一半。

segments.en: So the problem is always putting them back together again, right?
segments.zh: 所以问题总是把它们重新组合在一起，对吧？

segments.en: Exactly, so you can take it apart, but then you put it back together and there's always a screw missing or a screw that's extra or two or three parts.
segments.zh: 没错，拆开是可以，可是再装回去时，总是会少一颗螺丝，或者多出一颗螺丝，甚至多出两三个零件。

segments.en: Not a good sign.
segments.zh: 不是一个好兆头。

segments.en: Alright, so we've taken a look at a lot of great words and phrases, so let's listen to this dialogue for the last time.
segments.zh: 好，我们已经学了很多有用的词汇和短语，现在最后再听一遍对话。

segments.en: Howdy.
segments.zh: 你好。

segments.en: Nice car.
segments.zh: 好车。

segments.en: What seems to be the problem?
segments.zh: 请问有什么问题？

segments.en: I don't know. This stupid old car started spewing white smoke and it just died on me.
segments.zh: 我也不知道。这辆破旧的车开始冒白烟，然后就突然熄火了。

segments.en: Luckily, I managed to start it up and drive it here.
segments.zh: 幸好我设法把车重新发动，开到了这里。

segments.en: What do you think it is?
segments.zh: 你认为它是什么？

segments.en: Not sure yet.
segments.zh: 还不确定。

segments.en: How about you pop the hood and we can take a look?
segments.zh: 你把引擎盖拿出来，我们可以看看吗？

segments.en: Mmm, doesn't look good.
segments.zh: 嗯，看起来不太好。

segments.en: What do you mean?
segments.zh: 你是什么意思？

segments.en: My daddy gave me this car for my birthday last month.
segments.zh: 这辆车是上个月爸爸送我的生日礼物。

segments.en: It's brand new.
segments.zh: 这是全新的。

segments.en: Well, missy, the white smoke that you saw is steam from the radiator.
segments.zh: 嗯，小姐，你看到的白烟是散热器的蒸汽。

segments.en: You overheated your engine so now the pistons are busted and so is your transmission.
segments.zh: 您的发动机过热，因此现在活塞被破坏，您的变速箱也是如此。

segments.en: You should have called us and we could have towed you over here when your car died.
segments.zh: 车熄火时你就该打电话给我们，我们可以把车拖过来。

segments.en: Ugh, so how long is this going to take?
segments.zh: 呃，这需要多长时间？

segments.en: An hour?
segments.zh: 一个小时？

segments.en: I'm afraid a bit more than that.
segments.zh: 恐怕得更久一些。

segments.en: We need to order the spare parts, take apart your electrical system, fuel pump and engine, and then put it back together again.
segments.zh: 我们需要订购备件，把你的电路系统、燃油泵和发动机拆开，再重新装好。

segments.en: You're going to have to leave it here for at least two weeks.
segments.zh: 您将不得不将其留在这里至少两周。

segments.en: What?
segments.zh: 什么？

segments.en: How am I supposed to go to school?
segments.zh: 我该怎么去上学？

segments.en: Or go shopping?
segments.zh: 还是去购物？

segments.en: This is not happening.
segments.zh: 这没有发生。

segments.en: Alright, so car trouble. Have you ever had any very serious car trouble or something weird happened to your car?
segments.zh: 好，说到汽车故障，你有没有遇到过特别严重的故障，或者车上发生过什么怪事？

segments.en: Actually, the week before I decided to leave Chicago, I had this 1991 Honda Civic hatchback, so only two doors.
segments.zh: 有啊。在我决定离开芝加哥的前一周，当时我开的是一辆1991年的本田思域掀背车，只有两个车门。

segments.en: And I was driving home from work, I was on the highway, had the radio on, the windows open, and then doo doo doo doo, boom.
segments.zh: 我当时正开车下班回家，在高速公路上听着收音机，开着车窗，然后就“嘟嘟嘟嘟，砰”的一声。

segments.en: It died.
segments.zh: 它死了。

segments.en: It died in the middle of the highway during rush hour.
segments.zh: 它在高峰时段死在高速公路中间。

segments.en: So that's when there's tons of cars and I didn't know what to do.
segments.zh: 所以那是有大量汽车的时候，我不知道该怎么办。

segments.en: So I'm calling people and then all of a sudden I see someone tapping on my window.
segments.zh: 所以我打电话给人们，然后突然间我看到有人在敲我的窗户。

segments.en: And there's cars everywhere.
segments.zh: 到处都是汽车。

segments.en: And it's this guy.
segments.zh: 而且是这个人。

segments.en: And he's like, listen, do you need a hand? I said yes.
segments.zh: 他就像，听着，你需要一只手吗？ 我说是的。

segments.en: So I put the car in neutral so that there's no brake. And he pushed it to a side road and gave me a ride home.
segments.zh: 于是我把车挂到空挡，让它能推得动。他把车推到旁边的小路上，又开车送我回家。

segments.en: No way.
segments.zh: 不会吧。

segments.en: He was the coolest guy, he was so nice.
segments.zh: 他是最酷的人，他很好。

segments.en: And he was just there with his truck, he's a gardener, and just gave me a ride home.
segments.zh: 他只是带着他的卡车在那里，他是一名园丁，只是送我一程回家。

segments.en: It was super, super cool.
segments.zh: 超级超级酷。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: And so it turns out my engine died. No, the engine was new, it was the transmission, it was shot.
segments.zh: 所以事实证明我的引擎死了。 不，发动机是新的，它是变速箱，它被击中了。

segments.en: It was totally broken.
segments.zh: 它完全坏了。

segments.en: Wow.
segments.zh: 哇。

segments.en: But I was very lucky to have such a kind person.
segments.zh: 但我很幸运有这样一个善良的人。

segments.en: Yeah, that's a good story because usually people are too afraid or maybe a little bit reluctant to stop and see if you're okay or if you need a ride or something.
segments.zh: 是啊，这个故事真好。因为人们通常会害怕，或者不太愿意停车看看你有没有事、需不需要搭车之类的。

segments.en: Because you can't really trust people these days.
segments.zh: 因为这些天你不能真正相信别人。

segments.en: But it's good.
segments.zh: 但这很好。

segments.en: Once I saw somebody on the side of the road that had a flat tire, it was two girls and they didn't know what to do.
segments.zh: 有一次，我看到路边有人爆胎了，是两个女孩，她们不知道该怎么办。

segments.en: So I was passing by.
segments.zh: 所以我路过。

segments.en: It was actually raining.
segments.zh: 其实是在下雨。

segments.en: And I was like, hey, do you guys need a hand?
segments.zh: 我当时想，嘿，你们需要一只手吗？

segments.en: And they're like, yeah, please.
segments.zh: 他们就像，是的，拜托。

segments.en: We can't locate my dad or whatever.
segments.zh: 我们找不到我爸爸什么的。

segments.en: So I was like, changing the tire, it's not a big deal, right?
segments.zh: 所以我想，换轮胎，这没什么大不了的，对吧？

segments.en: And they wanted to tip me, they wanted to give me some money.
segments.zh: 他们想给我小费，他们想给我一些钱。

segments.en: Are you serious?
segments.zh: 你是认真的吗？

segments.en: They're like, oh, please take this, you're so kind, your time, and you're all wet.
segments.zh: 他们就像，哦，请接受这个，你很善良，你的时间，你都湿透了。

segments.en: And I'm like, no, no, don't worry about it.
segments.zh: 我想，不，不，不要担心。

segments.en: No, it's just a nice thing to do.
segments.zh: 不用谢，这只是举手之劳。

segments.en: If you know anything about cars, I mean, or if you can offer someone a lift.
segments.zh: 如果您对汽车有所了解，我的意思是，或者您是否可以为某人提供电梯。

segments.en: I know it's not terribly safe to ride with strangers, but this guy totally helped me out.
segments.zh: 我知道和陌生人一起骑车并不是很安全，但这家伙完全帮助了我。

segments.en: Nice. All right. Well, maybe you guys have some cool or maybe some interesting stories of what's happened with your cars or maybe you've helped somebody out.
segments.zh: 真好。也许你们也有一些有趣的经历，比如车出了什么事，或者曾经帮助过别人。

segments.en: So come to our website at EnglishPod.com and let us know.
segments.zh: 因此，请访问我们的网站 englishpod.com 并告诉我们。

segments.en: And of course, if you have any questions about the vocabulary or phrases that you heard today, please ask away.
segments.zh: 当然，如果你对今天听到的词汇或短语有任何问题，尽管提问。

segments.en: Don't hesitate.
segments.zh: 不要犹豫。

segments.en: And, well, again, we hope to see you on the website.
segments.zh: 而且，我们再次希望在网站上见到您。

segments.en: All right. We'll see you guys there.
segments.zh: 好的。 我们会在那里见到你们。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
